definitions.explanation: An area close to a reference point. As a noun, refers to the surrounding area.
Approximately or almost a certain amount.

examples.japanese: この{近|ちか}くに{住|す}んでいます。
{学校|がっこう}の{近|ちか}くにコンビニがあります。
examples.english: There's a convenience store near the school.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{近|ちか}くで{子|こ}どもたちが{遊|あそ}んでいます。
examples.english: Children are playing near the park.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{家|いえ}の{近|ちか}くには{大|おお}きな{図書館|としょかん}があって、{毎週|まいしゅう}{本|ほん}を{借|か}りに{行|い}っています。
examples.english: There's a big library near my house, and I go there every week to borrow books.

examples.japanese: {千|せん}{円|えん}{近|ちか}くかかった。
examples.english: It cost nearly a thousand yen.

examples.japanese: {二|に}{時間|じかん}{近|ちか}く{待|ま}ちました。
examples.english: I waited for nearly two hours.

examples.japanese: {五十|ごじゅう}{人|にん}{近|ちか}くが{集|あつ}まった。
この{仕事|しごと}を{終|お}わらせるのに{一|いち}{週間|しゅうかん}{近|ちか}くかかりました。
examples.english: It took nearly a week to finish this work.

examples.japanese: {百万|ひゃくまん}{円|えん}{近|ちか}くも{使|つか}ってしまったので、{貯金|ちょきん}がなくなってしまいました。
examples.english: I spent nearly a million yen, so my savings are gone.

notes: {近|ちか}く is the noun form of {近|ちか}い (close, near). When describing location, use [place]の{近|ちか}く (near [place]). この{近|ちか}く means 'near here' or 'in this area.' It can also mean 'nearly' or 'close to' when used with numbers or amounts.
